rows.source_body_exact: Euclidean Spin(4) is decomposed into two chiral SU(2) factors in the Euclidean-first proposal.

The two factors receive distinct gravitational/spacetime and internal-gauge roles. W01 §3 contrasts earlier cited [3] and [30] proposals gauging SU(2) and Lorentz SL(2,C) inside complexified Spin(4,C) with Woit's Euclidean Spin(4) approach. Its two Euclidean factors are not interchanged: SU(2)_L is an INTERNAL WEAK YANG–MILLS gauge factor, while SU(2)_R is the SPACETIME factor whose chiral spin connection is used in the proposed gravitational sector. Both statements are source attribution and proposed roles, not a qualified interacting unification.

Recovering Lorentz signature requires an imaginary-time-direction degree of freedom assigned a Higgs role. W01 §3 explicitly assumes a NONZERO distinguished imaginary-time vector e_0 in Hom(S_R,S_L) to reconstruct the proposed Minkowski theory. Choosing e_0 identifies a vector x through the e_0-relative element e_0^(-1)*x in Hom(S_R,S_R); the source PRINTS e_0^(-1)*x -> g_R*e_0^(-1)*g_L^(-1)*g_L*x*g_R^(-1) = g_R*e_0^(-1)*x*g_R^(-1). For x in the e_0 direction this relative element is invariant; for spatial x it is invariant under SU(2)_L, transforms as an E3 vector under SU(2)_R, and S_R is the spin representation of the spatial SO(3) double cover SU(2)_R. Preserve inverse, factor order, e_0 choice and the two CONDITIONAL cases rather than asserting an e_0-independent isomorphism.
Projective twistor space is the proposed natural base of the Euclidean-first theory.

rows.source_body_exact: The 2023 formulation replaces the chirally symmetric complex-spacetime description with a purely right-handed Lorentz action.
In that formulation, Euclidean left-handed spinors acquire an internal SU(2) role.
A distinguished Euclidean vector can reconstruct an isomorphism between left-handed and conjugate right-handed spinors, relating asymmetric and symmetric descriptions.
The usual Wick rotation of a single Weyl field creates a Euclidean chirality/doubling problem.
W04a proposes using only the right-handed spinor kind for spacetime vectors in both Minkowski and Euclidean signatures.
Under W04a, SU(2)_R acts geometrically and SU(2)_L is available as an internal symmetry.
Twistor space is C^4 / projective CP^3 with an SU(2,2) real form giving positive, negative, and null/boundary orbits for the Minkowski picture.
Euclidean spacetime is associated with extra fibration/real-structure data rather than the same real form as Minkowski spacetime.

W04c explicitly records a change from Euclidean-first to Minkowski-twistor-first foundational viewpoint. The March 10, 2026 W04c author post explicitly motivates this proposed Penrose-twistor plus Wick-rotation viewpoint by unresolved conventional Standard-Model spacetime/Wick difficulties and an author-stated research priority. This is motivation and an unverified priority judgement, not a theorem or a final current formulation.

In W04c, Wick rotation becomes a gauge-like extra choice, and the left chiral symmetry is interpreted internally before that choice. Its Wick rotation is described as LIKE a gauge choice, breaking the left chiral symmetry after choosing a CP1 fibration/imaginary-time normal direction; the source does not establish a literal physical gauge-equivalence operation.

W04c leaves the electroweak/Higgs completion of the revised viewpoint unresolved. The March 10 post expressly says large parts of the physical construction are missing: the author has made slow progress, does not here develop quantum gravity, and continues to work out how to formulate the proposed holomorphic quantum field theory. These are dated source-negative completion claims, not proof of impossibility.

W04d identifies complex-time holomorphy / boundary values as the essence of Wick rotation and says there is no distinguished Euclidean target without extra structure. Source W04d explicitly uses positive-energy (U(z)=e^{-izH}) with (z=t+is), holomorphy in the lower half-plane for (s<0), and a choice of line into that region; this is author-proposed Wick-rotation interpretation, not a complete new analytic continuation theorem.
W04d explicitly states that the exact new Wick-rotation implementation remains unresolved.
W04e says the author's interpretation is still changing and therefore later claims must remain revision-scoped.

W04e proposes a new conjugation-like structure interchanging positive/negative imaginary-time sectors while preserving a Lorentzian-chiral subspace. In his July 10, 2026 reply to the notes, Woit explicitly limits his immediate goal to **local four-dimensional QFT**, saying reconstruction on S4 would suffice for local physics and global four-manifold topology is not central to that goal. He is NOT trying to obtain a topological field theory (though one might appear incidentally). He requires an as-yet unconstructed extra conjugation structure on a Riemannian manifold and its twistor/projective-spin bundle, interchanging imaginary-time signs while retaining a Lorentzian-chiral subspace. His statement of not knowing prior work is explicitly limited by not having investigated thoroughly, not a universal novelty claim.

In Euclidean twistor geometry, a spacetime point is represented by a twistor P1. W05 §1 specifies the twistor P1 as the Riemann sphere together with the antipodal real structure and REPORTS a physical interpretation as the sphere of light rays through its corresponding spacetime point. The author's statement is Euclidean-signature scoped, not experimental proof, nor an identity between Euclidean twistor and Minkowski projective-dual real forms.

W05 presents the twistor P1 as a geometric avatar of quaternions. W05 says in its ABSTRACT that the notes are PURELY EXPOSITORY and that the twistor P1 is OFTEN a geometric avatar of quaternions; this is not a universal equation or a new Woit-original quaternion theorem. The Introduction also gives Simpson's Hodge-equivariant-bundle context, a Fargues–Fontaine finite-prime versus infinite-prime ANALOGY connected with Fargues and Scholze, Woit's earlier twistor-unification paper [19] as cited motivation, and explicit uncertainty as to the recurrence's deeper significance. Hyperkähler geometry and metaplectic canonical quantization appear as further cited contexts, not automatically equivalent mathematical systems or an established physical unification.

W01 fixes the Euclidean vector real form inside M(2,C) by the Pauli-matrix map, with determinant equal to positive Euclidean norm squared and an equivalent quaternion presentation with the quaternion norm x conjugate(x), with x a quaternion here rather than the distinct matrix carrier. W01 §2.1 prints the exact Euclidean matrix model x=x0*1-i(x1*sigma1+x2*sigma2+x3*sigma3), |x|^2=det(x), and the quaternion coordinate model x=x0*1+x1*i+x2*j+x3*k with |x|^2=x*conjugate(x). The preceding token KAPPA(x) is NOT the source-printed quaternion conjugate and is superseded here, not treated as a new operation.

W01 represents Spin(4) by independent left/right SU(2)=Sp(1) actions, with the Euclidean vector action x -> g_L x g_R^{-1}; the two factors are structurally independent in Euclidean signature. W01 §2.1 explicitly prints x maps to g_L*x*g_R^(-1) for Euclidean SU(2) left/right factors and says (g_L,g_R) and (-g_L,-g_R) determine the same SO(4) rotation, giving the source Spin(4) double-cover claim. The sign-paired representatives are not identical Spin-group elements. In the quaternion presentation SU(2)=Sp(1) is the unit-quaternion group with independent left and right multiplication and the imaginary-time coordinate maps to the identity. W01 §2.1 also singles out DIMENSION FOUR as an exceptional rotation-group factorization: in the author's words, rotations are not a simple group there but have the stated two-factor structure. This is conserved as Woit's dimension-scoped explanatory assertion, not an independently established classification theorem or a literal identity of SO(4) with SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R.

W01 identifies the common complexification of Euclidean, Minkowski, and split-signature four-vector spaces with M(2,C)=Hom(S_R,S_L), while retaining different real-form/action constraints for each signature. W01 separately prints the Minkowski embedding x=-i(x0*1+x1*sigma1+x2*sigma2+x3*sigma3) with determinant -x0^2+x1^2+x2^2+x3^2; the split E(2,2) model consists of REAL 2x2 matrices [[x0+x3,x1+x2],[x1-x2,x0-x3]] with determinant x0^2-x1^2+x2^2-x3^2. All three real spaces complexify to M(2,C), but they do not carry the same real-form constraint. The printed Minkowski Lorentz action is x maps to inverse(adjoint(g)) * x * inverse(g) for g in SL(2,C); the split-signature Spin(2,2)=SL(2,R)_L x SL(2,R)_R action is x maps to g_L*x*inverse(g_R). These typed group actions differ from the Euclidean Spin(4) real-form action, even though complexification is shared. W01 §2.2 separately states spinor carriers S_R,S_L with complexified vectors Hom(S_R,S_L), using R2 in split E(2,2) but C2 for E4 and E3,1. In Euclidean E4 the two spinor spaces transform independently, whereas Minkowski SL(2,C) action g on S_R forces the (g^dagger)^(-1) action on S_L. A twistor spacetime point is a C2 plane S_R inside T=C4, with its point-relative quotient S_L=T/S_R and tangent Hom(S_R,S_L). The complex Grassmannian G_2,4(C) carries the SL(4,C) conformal action with source-ordered real subgroup/compactification correspondences Spin(5,1)/E4/S4, Spin(4,2)/E3,1/(S3×S1), Spin(3,3)/E2,2/G_2,4(R); do not equate the real forms or promote source claims to new proofs.

W01's frame-bundle description distinguishes spin-connection one-forms omega from canonical/frame one-forms e, takes e and omega as the fundamental Palatini fields, and writes the action as the integral of epsilon_ABCD e^A wedge e^B wedge Omega^CD(omega); its equations of motion are obtained by varying omega^AB, which gives de^A + omega^A_B wedge e^B = 0 and thereby the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection determined by e, and by varying e^A, which gives the Einstein equations in terms of e. Its printed source action is precisely integral_M epsilon_ABCD e^A wedge e^B wedge Omega^CD(omega), where Omega(omega) denotes curvature of the spin connection, not an independent arbitrary field. Varying omega^AB gives the source-printed torsion equation de^A+omega^A_B wedge e^B=0; varying e^A separately gives Einstein equations. No generic zero-stationarity operator or variation-direction carrier is claimed.

W01 decomposes spin connection, curvature, and two-forms into chiral/Hodge sectors; the right and left connection-curvature pairs act on S_R and S_L respectively. The printed chiral decomposition is spin(4)=su(2)_R direct-sum su(2)_L; omega=omega_R+omega_L; Omega=Omega_R(omega_R)+Omega_L(omega_L); two-forms split Lambda^2(M)=Lambda^2_+(M) direct-sum Lambda^2_-(M), with Lambda^2_+ subset Hom(S_R,S_R) and Lambda^2_- subset Hom(S_L,S_L). Finally Omega(omega)=Omega_(+,R)(omega)+Omega_(+,L)(omega)+Omega_(-,R)(omega)+Omega_(-,L)(omega). Each sign/chiral subscript is a source role, not an interchangeable normalization.

For a torsion-free connection W01 states the vacuum Einstein condition as vanishing of a specified mixed/chiral curvature component and motivates a chiral formulation using only the right-handed connection/curvature sector; the omitted left connection becomes unconstrained if torsion is allowed. W01's exact torsion-free vacuum Einstein condition is Omega_(-,R)(omega)=0, and W01 separately prints its implication Omega_(+,L)(omega)=0. A third distinct source statement says solutions with Omega_(-,L)=0 will be self-dual/half-flat. These are not three interchangeable vanishing conditions and the first is conditional on torsion freedom. Chiral gravitational action replaces Omega by Omega_R, with the omitted omega_L left unconstrained only if torsion is allowed.

W01 constructs the weak SU(2)_L gauge sector from the left spin connection and uses the imaginary-time component of the canonical one-form as a Higgs candidate; it explicitly records the missing electroweak U(1) and SU(2)_R-invariance problems that motivate the twistor-space reformulation. W01 §3.2 separately says the proposed SU(2)_L weak connection omega_L and imaginary-time component of the canonical one-form as Higgs could be assigned the usual Standard Model Yang–Mills and Higgs kinetic/potential dynamics (an author claim, not a demonstrated complete model). It then lists two explicit objections: the electroweak extra U(1) is not yet supplied by SU(2)_L alone; and the Higgs one-form transforms nontrivially under BOTH SU(2)_L and SU(2)_R although the author wants invariance under SU(2)_R. W01 says the extra U(1) SHOULD combine with SU(2)_L to give U(2), with the Higgs in the defining complex C2 representation. The author points forward to a twistor-space formulation as a proposed solution, not a completed source-local proof in §3.2.

Its next intermediate display literally uses (C_-1 TENSOR C3_(+1/3)) TENSOR (C2_0 DIRECT-SUM C_-1 DIRECT-SUM C_+1), not the direct-sum first factor previously transcribed; its following six weighted components are printed with three ⊕ and then two + separators in that order. Preserve all source operators, signs, relative U(1) weights, six-component ordering, and the distinct printed carrier claim. The displayed intermediate tensor is not silently replaced by a mathematically repaired direct sum, and no completed physical dynamics is inferred.

Appendix B treats reconstruction of physical states from Euclidean data as requiring a chosen imaginary-time half-space/reflection and states that the resulting distinction between positive and negative imaginary time breaks SO(4) despite SO(4)-invariant Schwinger functions.
